intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities-2 (NDOABA2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the BORCS5 gene (616598) on chromosome 12p13.2.

paragraphs.text: NDOABA2 is a severe autosomal recessive disorder that has been described as neuroaxonal dystrophy with osteopetrosis. It was identified prenatally in affected fetuses by cerebral ventriculomegaly and agenesis of the corpus callosum. At autopsy, the fetuses had facial dysmorphism, osteopetrosis, and neuropathologic findings consistent with neuroaxonal dystrophy (Fisher et al., 2025).

Autopsies of both fetuses showed similar abnormalities, including facial dysmorphism, osteopetrosis, and neuropathologic findings consistent with neuroaxonal dystrophy.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sib fetuses with NDOABA2, born to consanguineous Pakistani parents, Fisher et al. (2025) used trio exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.283C-T transition in exon 3 of the BORCS5 gene, resulting in an arg95-to-ter (R95X) substitution. Each parent was heterozygous for the mutation. One of the affected fetuses was also homozygous for a missense variant of uncertain significance in the SCYL2 gene (616365), c.902G-A, resulting in an arg301-to-his (R301H) substitution, for which both parents were heterozygous. Because the autopsy findings in the 2 sibs were identical, Fisher et al. (2025) raised the possibility that the SCYL2 variant did not contribute to the phenotype.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sib fetuses with NDOABA2, born to consanguineous Pakistani parents, Fisher et al. (2025) used trio exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.283C-T transition in exon 3 of the BORCS5 gene, resulting in an arg95-to-ter (R95X) substitution. Each parent was heterozygous for the mutation. Prenatally, the fetuses had cerebral ventriculomegaly and agenesis of the corpus callosum. Autopsy showed facial dysmorphism, osteopetrosis, and neuropathologic findings consistent with neuroaxonal dystrophy. One of the fetuses was also homozygous for a missense variant of uncertain significance in SCYL2 (R301H). The authors raised the possibility that this variant did not contribute to the phenotype, because the autopsy findings in the 2 sibs were identical.
